key_insight: Combining polynomial reduced-order models with quantum transport preserves nonlinear drift while making per-step rotation counts scale polylogarithmically with grid cells at fixed model dimension and polynomial degree.
engineering_relevance: Reduced-model polynomial degree becomes a practical design variable for balancing flow-model accuracy against early fault-tolerant quantum hardware costs.
method: Fit polynomial reduced-order models using sparse identification of nonlinear dynamics.
Implement Koopman–von Neumann transport with Walsh-synthesized quantum circuits.
Estimate end-to-end runtime and physical qubits using surface-code resource models.
evidence_signal: For a saturating cylinder wake, the estimated cost is 1.62 hours on about 560,000 physical qubits for 1% relative RMS field error against the radial model; IBM experiments demonstrate nonlinear radial transport with reference-circuit noise mitigation.
watch_item: The fault-tolerant results are resource estimates rather than demonstrated end-to-end performance, and the reported 1% error is relative to the radial model, not the full flow.
paper_title: Nonlinearity-preserving quantum simulation of flows in the early fault-tolerant regime
